    Species distribution model specification

    Source: R/parsnip-models.R
    inv_sdm.Rd

    inv_sdm() defines a presence-background (or presence-absence) species distribution model for use with the tidymodels framework. Predictors are standardised and expanded into polynomial terms of degree degree (degree 2 gives the classic quadratic response curves). Two engines are available:

    Usage

    inv_sdm(mode = "classification", engine = "glm", degree = NULL)

    Arguments

    mode

    Must be "classification".

    engine

    "glm" or "iwlr".

    degree

    Polynomial degree of each predictor (1 or 2, or higher).

    Value

    A model specification of class inv_sdm.

    Details

    • "glm": logistic regression (binomial GLM) of presence against background or absence. Probabilities are probabilities of presence under the sampling design.

    • "iwlr": infinitely weighted logistic regression (Fithian and Hastie 2013). Background rows get a large weight (bg_weight, an engine argument, default 100), so slope estimates converge on those of an inhomogeneous Poisson process, the model underlying Maxent. Predictions are the relative intensity mapped to 0 to 1 with a complementary log-log link: a relative suitability index, not a probability of presence.

    The outcome must be a two-level factor whose first level is the presence, following the yardstick convention. Class predictions use the threshold that maximises the True Skill Statistic on the training data (Liu et al. 2005), which suits the low prevalence of presence-background data far better than 0.5. Set the engine argument threshold to a number to override it, for example set_engine("glm", threshold = 0.3).

    References

    Fithian, W. and Hastie, T. (2013). Finite-sample equivalence in statistical models for presence-only data. Annals of Applied Statistics, 7, 1917-1939. doi:10.1214/13-AOAS667

    Liu, C., Berry, P. M., Dawson, T. P. and Pearson, R. G. (2005). Selecting thresholds of occurrence in the prediction of species distributions. Ecography, 28, 385-393. doi:10.1111/j.0906-7590.2005.03957.x

    Examples

    spec <- inv_sdm(degree = 2) |> parsnip::set_engine("glm")
fit <- parsnip::fit(spec, presence ~ temp + rain + forest, data = inv_sdm_data)
predict(fit, inv_sdm_data[1:5, ], type = "prob")
#> # A tibble: 5 × 2
#>   .pred_presence .pred_background
#>            <dbl>            <dbl>
#> 1      0.0000644            1.000
#> 2      0.00121              0.999
#> 3      0.0421               0.958
#> 4      0.00241              0.998
#> 5      0.0219               0.978

iw <- inv_sdm() |> parsnip::set_engine("iwlr", bg_weight = 100)
parsnip::fit(iw, presence ~ temp + rain, data = inv_sdm_data)
#> parsnip model object
#> 
#> <inv_sdm_fit> iwlr species distribution model, degree 2
#> Predictors: temp and rain
#> Class threshold: 0.0897
